text:
think there’s a lot of truth to the idea that  esp in a work setting, ppl are always going to remember you as their first impression

so if u were the young buck getting everyone coffees, doing sandwich runs etc, it becomes hard to escape from that “image” even as u advance

not so much a question of right or wrong as much as it is, just an unalterable aspect of human nature - ie a parents’ child-like image of a grown human

I bring this up mostly because if u feel like ur in a position where u aren’t getting the respect u deserve…u may not be wrong to feel the way u do.

obviously the skill and performance have to be real, and u can’t misconstrue a perceived lack of respect for a merited lack of respect (u just aren’t as good as u think at the job).

but if the talent is real, there is a valid argument to be made that sometimes u have to switch firms to get the title and comp that u rightfully deserve.

v situation-specific…talk to someone irl who u trust on these matters + knows ur character, to see what they think.
